Our independent research path asks whether a fixed, input-independent network of globally overlapping, possibly nonunitary quasiseparable stages with arbitrary permutations can compute all DFT outputs on fresh arbitrary inputs in `o(N log N)` charged arithmetic, ideally `O(N)`. We do not count caching, many queries sharing factors, threads, numerical near-matches, or a dressed ordinary FFT as a win. All previous code and its 29 tests are preserved recursively in `prior_checkpoint/`.

Single-threaded CPython, warm precomputed plans, fresh full-length modular inputs, identical exact outputs; comparisons are against our own Python NTT, not a tuned native FFT. Coefficient, permutation-index and twiddle preparation are counted separately in code and would only worsen the dressed path.

- Zai Yang, Sikai Ge, and Wenlong Wang, *Pursuing the Limit of Chirp Parameter Identifiability: A Computational Approach* (2025 preprint; a 2026 journal version was found). The inspected preprint allows different continuous chirp rates, encodes identifiability as uniqueness of a rank-constrained structured matrix problem, and develops numerical optimization. Its task is different from exact membership recognition on the finite roots-of-unity grid. In particular, do not claim that N ≥ 3r is a new universal identifiability threshold or that the returned representation is always unique. [Preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01286), Theorems 2 and 4; [full text](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.01286v1).
